en: Sutta Nipāta 5.17 Piṅgiya-māṇava-pucchā “I am old,
weak, and my complexion has faded;”
(Thus spoke the Venerable Piṅgiya:
"The guide is not pure, nor is hearing it secure;
may I not perish, deluded, along the way."
"Teach me the Dhamma so that I may understand it—
the relinquishing of birth and aging here and now.
"Having seen beings being tormented among forms..."
(Piṅgiyāni, said the Blessed One:
"People who are heedless are tormented by forms;
therefore, Piṅgiya, you must be heedful."
“May you abandon form so that there is no further becoming.
“The four cardinal directions, the four intermediate directions,
above and below— these are the ten directions.”
There is nothing in the world that has not been seen, heard, sensed, or cognized by you;
teach me the Dhamma so that I may understand it.
“The abandoning here of birth and old age.
“Beholding mankind overcome by craving,” said the Blessed One, Piṅgiya.
“Tormented by fever and overcome by old age,
therefore you too, Piṅgiya, being diligent,
should abandon craving so as not to be born again.”
The sixteenth is the inquiry of the young brahmin Piṅgiya.
